newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac doubts Italy will be in first EMU group.
newsitem.headline: Chirac doubts Italy will be in first EMU group.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Tuesday that Italy may not be among the first group of countries to join a single European currency in 1999.

Chirac told businessmen on a tour of northern France: "Things are going to go pretty quickly now, on January 1, 1999, for some countries which will have made the effort to clean up their economic and financial situation...It may take a little bit longer for those who are further behind, like Italy."

Chirac's comment was a blow to the Italian government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi, which has set its sights on joining European monetary union from the outset by adopting an austerity budget for 1997. It set the scene for a possible clash at a Franco-Italian summit in Naples on Thursday night and Friday.

Speaking in a depressed textile town, the president said France had suffered from a devaluation of the Italian lira, the British pound and the Spanish peseta, which had hit its textile industry harder than southeast Asian imports.
"(It is) quite obvious that the lira's movement is completely incompatible with a single European market, even if it has rebounded slightly recently," Chirac said.
A fixed link between the euro and the currencies of non-founder members of the European unit was an "unavoidable" necessity, he added.
